attempts.label: CRCNS:ear-1
attempts.entry_title: Voltage sensing in the lateral membrane of guinea pig outer hair cells (Farrell et al. 2020)
attempts.summary: Five of the paper's central findings held up in this data, including the voltage-sensitivity and half-activation-voltage (V0.5) differences between pigmented and albino cells and the fit of V0.5 against charge density (Fig. 3a). Several of the model's quantitative claims, such as the sensor-area range and the two capacitance limits, did not reproduce, and the sequencing and cross-species claims could not be tested. Most of these rest on a per-cell lateral-wall capacitance that the dataset does not store, so the agent rebuilt it from a cited method. Evidence for two hyperpolarized states is mixed: the slope near -1/2 holds, but the mean slope and the capacitance limits fall just outside tolerance. The XE991 voltage-clamp improvement, the V0.5 length gradient and the equality of the two colonies' V0.5-capacitance slopes also failed. The sequencing, protein-model and other-species claims need data outside the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Farrell, Skidmore, Rajasekharan and Brownell (2020) on CRCNS data set ear-1, which holds the whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings of 89 guinea pig outer hair cells with the per-cell values the authors derived. It compares the charge, voltage sensitivity and V0.5 between colonies, cochlear regions and bath conditions, and refits the relations of V0.5 with charge density that the paper's model rests on. The sequencing, the protein model and the values from other rodents are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: The data set holds the paper's 89 OHCs, 39 from adult males (17 albino, 22 pigmented), 21 from prepubertal males (15 albino, 6 pigmented), 28 from prepubertal females (10 albino, 18 pigmented) and 1 pigmented cell from an adult female.

outcomes.quote: Electrophysiological data were obtained from 89 OHCs, namely 39 (17 albino and 22 pigmented) from adult males, 21 (15 albino and 6 pigmented) from prepubertal males, 28 (10 albino and 18 pigmented) from prepubertal females, and 1 pigmented from an adult female
outcomes.notes: All eight group counts match the paper (17 and 22 adult males, 15 and 6 prepubertal males, 10 and 18 prepubertal females, 1 pigmented adult female); 42 albino and 47 pigmented cells. 3 cells have 10 mM chloride, 20 have XE991 (all stored as 60 uM), 81 have Rs < 10 MOhm (all 89 below 12 MOhm), and recordings were made 47 to 182 min after death.
deviations: The HDF5 maturity `juvenile` (10 males) is read as prepubertal, as the original MATLAB files put these cells in the prepubertal-male file.

deviations: CL is recomputed as the mean C over 0.09 to 0.15 V, the range the Methods give for Rm and Rs where there is no measurable voltage-dependent capacitance (Methods, Whole-cell patch-clamp, paragraph 2); the paper's own linear region was picked by hand.

CLn is not stored and the paper gives no rule beyond the plateau (Results, Asymmetry of C versus V function, paragraph 1). Assumed: CLn is the mean C of the two most negative ramp points (this gives the Fig. S1 legend's 25.94 pF for its cell), and a cell has a plateau when the slope of C at or below -0.15 V is less than 0.4 of the steepest 5-point slope of the hyperpolarized flank, the fraction whose count is nearest the paper's 62 cells. This outcome does not rest on the CLn rule: the other reading (C at or below -0.15 V) gives 26.69 pF, also within 25.94 +/- 2.594 pF.

findings.statement: The data set stores CL, QTm, V0.5 and alphaB per cell, but not the lateral wall capacitance CLW, the stereocilia bundle capacitance CSB or the non-lateral-wall capacitance CNLW that the paper's Eq. 8a uses, so the paper's CLW and charge density cannot be taken from it. Computed here with the CSB rule of Corbitt et al. (2012) on the stored area, CLW reproduces the Fig. S1 legend's value (18.30 against 18.56 pF), but several results (the XE991 fits, the band of Fig. 1, the lower C_Leq limit) turn on the CLW of the smallest cells, which this rule makes as small as 0.48 pF.

The linear capacitance at negative voltages, CLn, and the rule for when it could be estimated are not stored; neither are the linear-region indices in the HDF5 files (the MATLAB files keep them as indposit_ramplin).

In every HDF5 file with DC steps (19 cells), `transformed data set/.../I_mean` has shape (N, 2) but stores its values in MATLAB column order (the N means, then the N SDs). Read as given, the mean and SD columns are interleaved; reshaped to (2, N) it equals the (mean, SD) columns of the original MATLAB files.
File sensory_cell_#52.h5 holds the membrane at +0.06 V before and after the ramp, where the stimulus description in every file says -0.06 V.

`cell_surface_area` follows two formulas, 2 pi r l for the 34 cells with a cell length and 2 pi r LW + 2 pi r^2 (with the lateral wall length) for 50 others, and the description does not say so or which length is which measurement; `cochlear_outer_hair_cell_length` is stored for 35 cells and `cochlear_outer_hair_cell_lateral_wall_length` for 83.

The cells behind the paper's tables are not marked. The data set gives 27 pigmented cells without XE991 with 144 mM chloride (paper 28), 17 pigmented XE991 cells with 144 mM chloride split 5 and 12 by region (Table 1 row a, 4 and 11), 69 Fig. 2 cells (legend 70), 46 cells for Fig. 3b by the rule used here (legend 44).
The original MATLAB field `toxins` labels 15 of the 20 XE991 cells `XE991` and 5 `yes`; the HDF5 files store 60 uM for all 20, while the Methods give 30 to 60 uM.

The `original cell number` is not unique: 13 numbers are used by two cells each, from different dates and mostly different researchers and colonies. The file number is the only unique identifier, and the paper names cells by original number (Fig. S1, cell 99).

Question for the paper's authors. How was CLn taken (which voltages, and what counted as having reached the hyperpolarized plateau, so that 62 cells qualify), and how was the per-cell CSB of Eq. 8 computed? The CLn rule assumed here (mean of the two most negative ramp points, plateau when the negative-end slope is below 0.4 of the steepest slope of the flank) gives 62 cells and the Fig. S1 legend's 25.94 pF, but the basal share of dC is 36.1%, not 21%. The CSB assumed here is the rule of Corbitt et al. (2012), bundle area min(0.07 AM, 140 um2) at 0.0075 pF/um2 with AM the stored cell surface area; it gives a root of 5.10 pF and the Fig. S1 cell CLW 18.30 pF (legend 18.56 pF). Was this the rule, and which area was AM? Were bins or groups with a large charge density left out of the Fig. 3a fits and the Fig. 4 groups, as the Fig. S4 fit leaves out Delta V min exp >= 0.4 V? Under the CSB rule assumed here, the two smallest XE991 cells form a bin of mean dVmin 0.80 V; with it the XE991 fit has an adjusted R2 of -43, without it all four of the paper's values are matched, and the lower C_Leq limit moves from 0.560 to 0.650 aF.

The largest conductance at V0.5 among XE991 cells is 8.5 nS from the DC steps and 7.0 nS from the admittance, about 25 times the 335 pS the paper reports; the unit or the measure in the paper may differ from the data set's.

entries.title: Voltage sensing in the lateral membrane of guinea pig outer hair cells (Farrell et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Farrell, Skidmore, Rajasekharan and Brownell (2020) on CRCNS data set ear-1, which holds the whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings of 89 guinea pig outer hair cells with the per-cell values the authors derived. It compares the charge, voltage sensitivity and V0.5 between colonies, cochlear regions and bath conditions, and refits the relations of V0.5 with charge density that the paper's model rests on. The sequencing, the protein model and the values from other rodents are not in the data set.
